title: Hosted API demo - Chat & text basics (streaming, params, retries) - VentraHealth
summary: 30-45 minute hosted API demo focused on chat/text generation basics: streaming responses, key params (temperature, top_p, max_tokens), and retry/backoff behavior. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated; strong security questions re: data retention and VPC options. Action items: send pricing, security whitepaper, and quickstart repo + sample benchmark script.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood Inference, AE for the VentraHealth account. Today Samira our SE will walk through a hosted API demo for chat/text basics. We have about 45 minutes, feel free to interrupt.
[00:12] Mark (VentraHealth - CTO): Hi Alex, Lina, Priyanka on from our side. We're mostly interested in latency and data controls, and cost perf.
[00:20] Samira (Redwood SE): Great, quick agenda we'll show the Console briefly, then live chat demo (streaming), talk params and retries, and finish with Q&A.
[00:35] Ben (VentraHealth): Quick note, we might ask about dedicated later but right now evaluating hosted for speed to market.
[00:42] Samira: Understood. Ok starting the Console apologies if the screen share lags. Here is the model catalog we typically recommend the curated open models or our verified profiles. Notice the streaming toggle in the request panel.
[01:10] Lina: Is streaming on by default? We want token-level latency for UI.
[01:15] Samira: Not default, you can enable streaming per request. Streaming uses server-sent events and sends chunks as tokens are generated. For React frontends we recommend our SDK streaming helper or using the SSE endpoint.
[01:28] Alex: Also mention that streaming reduces perceived latency for users you get first tokens much faster even if total generation time is same.
[01:36] Priyanka (Security): On retention, is there an option to disable logging of prompt/response? We have PHI concerns.
[01:44] Samira: Yes hosted API has a data retention flag: by default we retain logs for 30 days for debugging, but customers can opt out and we offer a no-retention toggle for keyed requests. For regulated customers we push Private/Dedicated options with customer-managed KMS. Small note: sometimes our docs show "KV cash" (typo) in older drafts, it's KV cache sorry for that.
[02:10] Mark: Cool. Can you demo a streaming chat example?
[02:14] Samira: Sure. I'll send a simple chat payload. (screen shows request) payload: {"model":"redwood-chat-v1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the recent clinical trial data..."}],"stream":true,"max_tokens":300} you'll see events arriving.
[02:35] [streaming partial tokens appear]
[02:38] Alex: You'll notice the first chunk arrives ~200ms after the prompt hits the server for shorter outputs, depends on model/seq length. For longer contexts it's a bit higher.
[02:52] Lina: What controls those numbers? batch size? hardware?
[02:55] Samira: It's a mix the model variant, batch shaping, and the sequence length. Our running runtime uses continuous batching and KV cache to keep latencies predictable. Also kernel selection matters for quantized variants.
[03:12] Ben: About parameters can you walk through temp, top_p, frequency_penalty? We want deterministic templates for system messages.
[03:18] Samira: Sure. Temperature controls randomness; top_p is nucleus sampling using both is redundant but possible. For deterministic outputs we set temperature 0, top_p 1, and also set max_tokens small. For system messages you'd typically use low temp and often pin examples.
[03:40] Alex: We also suggest using stop sequences and token limits to avoid runaway generations.
[03:46] Priyanka: How about retries? If the API returns 5xx, what does the client do?
[03:51] Samira: Our client libraries implement an exponential backoff with jitter. Default behavior is 3 retries for transient errors, and idempotency is handled via request IDs if you re-play completions. For streaming it's trickier we recommend checkpointing partial outputs and re-requesting with seed prompt + last confirmed token.
[04:15] Mark: Does Redwood do automatic retries for rate limits? Say we exceed QPS.
[04:20] Alex: The platform returns 429 with Retry-After header; our SDK will do exponential backoff. For high-throughput we recommend the Dedicated path or rate-limit keys per-route. There is also a built-in quota enforcement and soft-limits you can configure in the Console.
[04:38] Lina: On the SDK example, can you show code for a chat call?
[04:42] Samira: Yes here's a Node snippet: const resp = await client.chat.create({model: 'redwood-chat-v1', messages: msgs, temperature: 0.2, stream: true}); then pipe resp to an event handler. (note: rough paste transcript may mangle quotes)
[05:05] [small crosstalk: "uh-huh", "yeah"]
[05:10] Ben: Are there server-side hooks for function calling? We have structured outputs.
[05:14] Samira: We support function/tool calling you can register functions and the model will return a call which the runtime emits as structured JSON. Caveat: sometimes NLU detects similar names and we recommend schema enforcement.
[05:30] Priyanka: Security SAML/SSO and audit logs?
[05:34] Alex: Enterprise plans include SCIM, SSO, RBAC and audit logs. Private deployments can integrate with KMS/HSM. We'll attach SOC 2 and ISO cert pack in the follow-up.
[05:46] Mark: Latency SLOs for hosted?
[05:49] Samira: Our hosted 95th latency depends on selected model and region. For small chat messages we typically see 95th ~200-500ms for lightweight variants, heavier ~600-1200ms. We publish model profiles in the Console. For firm SLOs we recommend Dedicated with reserved GPUs.
[06:10] Lina: How does cost look for production usage? Token pricing?
[06:13] Alex: Pricing is per-token for generations and per-embedding for embeddings; we'll send the current price sheet. If you commit to Dedicated we'll provide reserved capacity pricing.
[06:25] Ben: Any gotchas when moving from hosted to dedicated? Data migrations?
[06:28] Samira: Mostly config: model pinning, quantization variant selection, and networking (VPC peering). Models can be the same binary but runtime config differs. We sometimes need to re-run a small benchmark because kernel selection can change perf.
[06:45] [~10 minute mark elided in transcript for brevity demo continues with a second chat turn: content trimmed...]
[16:50] Samira: Back to retries and deterministic tests for evals we recommend recording prompts and responses and running them through Redwood Optimize to catch regressions.
[17:02] Lina: Does Optimize integrate with our CI?
[17:06] Samira: Yes you can run evals programmatically and get regression alerts that tie to commit IDs.
[17:12] Mark: Quick question on data residency do you offer EU-only retention?
[17:17] Alex: Yes, we have region scoping for retention and region routing policies. For strict residency we recommend Private deployments or dedicated instances in the EU region.
[17:31] Priyanka: Ok thanks. On the streaming example I noticed occasional partial truncation what's the recommended client behavior?
[17:36] Samira: Clients should be robust to partial SSE events and reassemble tokens; if the connection drops you can re-request with an idempotent request id and the runtime will return the full completion if it's already completed (but that is not a strict guarantee for in-flight streams).
[17:57] Ben: Any examples of production customers in healthcare?
[18:01] Alex: We have several customers in healthtech on Dedicated/Private; we can share anonymized case studies and compliance references.
[18:10] [screen shows Console: quotas, tokens breakdown]
[18:15] Samira: One more practical: to reduce cost use prefix caching for repeated prompts and short-circuit when output matches templates. Also intelligent batch sizing in Redwood Optimize can reduce per-token cost.
[18:32] Lina: Is there an easy way to measure token breakdown per route?
[18:36] Alex: In the Console we show token-level cost per route and per token type. You can export reports to CSV.
[18:45] Priyanka: How about encryption at rest keys? Bring-your-own-KMS?
[18:49] Samira: BYOK is supported on Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports customer-managed keys for certain enterprise tiers; we'll clarify in the security pack.
[19:02] Mark: Ok, let's talk next steps.
[19:05] Alex: Quick recap: we'll send pricing, security whitepaper, sample quickstart repo and a benchmark script you can run against our hosted API to measure latency/cost. We'll also propose a pilot timeline.
[19:18] Lina: Can we get a scoped quote for 3 months of pilot with 50k tokens/day?
[19:23] Alex: Yes we'll include that in the pricing email.
[19:26] Priyanka: Also please include SOC2 docs and the EU data residency note.
[19:30] Alex: Will do. Any remaining technical Qs?
[19:34] Ben: One more how do you handle stuck generations? We saw in an earlier PoC a hung request.
[19:40] Samira: We have a request timeout and watchdog typically the client receives 504 after server-side timeout; the SDK will bubble that up and you can retry or fail-safe to a lighter model. For mission-critical flows we recommend fallback policy to a smaller variant.
[19:55] Mark: Perfect, thanks.
[20:00] Alex: Thanks everyone we'll follow up with materials.
[20:05] [call ends note: transcript auto-capture sometimes mislabels speakers, some punctuation missing]
